title: HF definition · 2026 universal framework
summary: The 2026 consensus groups HF into reduced, preserved and improved EF, moving beyond rigid EF cutoffs and describing improvement, remission and recovery trajectories.
population: Clinical HF assessment using symptoms, cardiac abnormalities and disease trajectory.
locator: 2026 universal definition: classification and disease-trajectory framework
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: Diagnostic framework, not a replacement set of drug recommendation classes.
The EF cutoffs used in Sage’s 2022 treatment pathways are source-specific treatment criteria, not an automated application of the 2026 definition.
Improvement does not establish durable recovery or permission to stop therapy.

title: MI definition · 2026 universal framework
summary: MI requires acute myocardial injury with evidence of ischemia. The 2026 definition distinguishes primary, secondary and procedure-related MI; troponin elevation alone is insufficient.
population: Diagnostic assessment of suspected myocardial injury or infarction.
locator: §5 Definition of myocardial infarction; §6 myocardial injury; classification framework
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: This prototype does not diagnose acute MI or assess emergency symptoms.
Secondary MI or myocardial injury does not by itself establish atherothrombotic ASCVD or an ACS antiplatelet indication.
Definition and treatment guidance have distinct roles; retain source-specific ACS/CCD eligibility.

title: HFmrEF · 2026 HFSA individualized GDMT framework
summary: Evaluate the cause and EF trajectory. The HFSA statement considers HFrEF-style quadruple therapy reasonable when individually appropriate, while acknowledging limited dedicated HFmrEF trials.
population: Adults with established HFmrEF in the statement's 41–49% treatment framework.
locator: Evaluation of HFmrEF / Figure 4; Management and Follow Up, concluding synthesis
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: Reference only; no automatic four-drug regimen. Review each agent's eligibility, current therapy, blood pressure, kidney function, potassium and contraindications.
The April 2026 statement's numerical EF treatment framework is not the June 2026 universal definition's complete classification.

title: ACS 2026 · preferred stool-based screening options
summary: Multitarget stool RNA is a preferred option every 3 years; original/next-generation stool DNA every 3 years and annual high-sensitivity FIT remain options.
population: Average-risk asymptomatic adults eligible for screening; age, health, prior results and life expectancy still govern continuation.
locator: Table 1, Preferred screening options; Table 2, stool-based tests
strength: ACS recommendation · no separate test-specific grade
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: Positive non-colonoscopy tests require timely colonoscopy; the narrative prefers completion within 6 months.
This does not apply to prior CRC/polyps, IBD, hereditary/strong family risk or prior abdominal/pelvic radiation.

title: ACS 2026 · blood-based testing when preferred options are not completed
summary: Blood-based screening is nonpreferred; consider only after preferred stool or visual testing is declined or not completed, with discussion of limitations.
population: Average-risk asymptomatic screening-eligible adults who decline or have not completed a preferred screening test.
locator: Table 1, Recommendation for blood-based colorectal cancer screening; Recommendations and Rationale
strength: ACS recommendation · no separate test-specific grade
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: Lower sensitivity for precancerous lesions and stage I cancer than preferred tests; a positive result needs colonoscopy.
Do not encode a 3-year blood-test interval as an ACS clinical recommendation: Table 1 identifies that as CMS coverage, with optimal interval unestablished.

title: VA/DoD · combination nicotine replacement
summary: For adults using tobacco, combination nicotine replacement is recommended over a single NRT product.
population: Adults using tobacco; treatment suitability and preferences reviewed.
locator: Table 4, recommendation 3: combination NRT over single NRT
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: Reference only; review product doses, contraindications and behavioral support.
National treatment recommendation does not establish local formulary authorization.

title: VA/DoD · varenicline among monotherapies
summary: Varenicline is recommended over other pharmacotherapy monotherapies for tobacco cessation.
population: Adults using tobacco for whom cessation pharmacotherapy is appropriate.
locator: Table 4, recommendation 4: varenicline over other monotherapies
evidenceNote: Original source system retained. No separate ACC/AHA COR or LOE inferred.
cautions: This compares monotherapies; it does not claim superiority over combination NRT.
Assess renal dosing, current medicines, prior treatment and contraindications. VA availability requires separate CFU/formulary review.
